title: Bann Valley & Killoquin
standfirst: Daniel and Thomas Glasgow are securely documented brothers in a wider Kilrea–Lisnagaver cluster. The generation above them, and Alexander’s place in the group, remain deliberately qualified.
question: Can estate and church records resolve the older Alexander-and-Rosanna generation and Alexander’s relationship to Daniel and Thomas?
answer: Daniel’s will calls Thomas his late brother and Daniel Neely his nephew; Daniel Neely’s marriage names Thomas as father. Alexander-951 may be their brother or cousin from shared locality and chronology, but no record states it. The older Alexander and Rosanna are a descendant tradition, not a contemporary parent record.

chapters.title: The proved sibling statement
body: Daniel's original 1871 will calls Thomas his late brother and names Daniel Neely Glasgow as his nephew. Daniel Neely's 1888 marriage names Thomas Glasgow, farmer, as father.
Together the records prove Daniel and Thomas were brothers; the will does not name their parents.

chapters.title: Alexander beside the brothers
body: Alexander and Thomas were similarly aged Presbyterian farmers whose families appear in nearby Killoquin and Lisnagaver settings, including the small 1851 enumeration cluster.
That cumulative pattern supports a possible brother-or-cousin placement; it is not an explicit sibling record. Alexander's son Robert's 1866 marriage does explicitly name Alexander as father.

chapters.title: The missing older generation
body: A descendant account names older Alexander and Rosanna as Thomas's parents, but provides no contemporary witness and does not establish Rosanna's surname.
Killoquin estate accounts for 1786–87 are targeted because tenant details might identify the prior generation; their contents have not been inspected.
